Q: Refresh only measures in Power BI A:

I have two ideas:

  1. to reduce the dataset only for development purposes to 10% of the original dataset - this will reduce the update time accordingly.

  2. to disable a heavy dataset update in powerquery, again, only for development time.

Not sure it can be called a "best practice", but it helps.

Q: Returning multiple values using Vlookup in excel A:

What a difference 10 years in Excel makes! This is easier to solve with array formulas that spill results.

First use IF to create a filtered list of results.

=IF(A2:A6=1,C2:C6,"")

Then use TEXT to format the list of results into dates.

This is important. If it isn't done the dates will be joined in the step as numbers.

=TEXT(IF(A2:A6=1,C2:C6,""),"dd/mm/yyyy")

Finally use TEXTJOIN to join the dates into a string in a single cell.

=TEXTJOIN(", ",TRUE,TEXT(IF(A2:A6=1,C2:C6,""),"dd/mm/yyyy"))

The separator is a comma and a space and the ignore_empty is set to TRUE.

Q: Connecting to Exchange 365 via SMTP OAuth A:

The 535 5.7.3 Authentication unsuccessful with SMTP + OAuth2 usually means the token is not acceptable for SMTP AUTH (wrong audience/scope/permission), or SMTP AUTH is still disabled at tenant/mailbox level, or the “username” you pass is not a pure email address.

Here are the most common fixes for your exact code/config.

1) Your token “resource/audience” is likely wrong

For SMTP AUTH with Exchange Online, Microsoft’s guidance uses the Outlook resource URL (for SMTP scope and .default audience). In their OAuth article they show SMTP scope as https://outlook.office.com/SMTP.Send and they also mention client-credentials as an alternative flow.

So change your token request scope

from:

https://outlook.office365.com/.default ❌

to:

https://outlook.office.com/.default ✅ (most commonly used for these legacy protocol tokens)

That mismatch alone can produce “auth unsuccessful”.

2) If you want “no user interaction”, you must use the correct application permission + admin consent

For app-only (client credentials), your Entra app must have the Exchange Online Application permission SMTP.SendAsApp (not Graph Mail.Send), and tenant admin consent must be granted. Microsoft explicitly lists “SMTP.SendAsApp” under Office 365 Exchange Online → Application permissions.

Also: in many orgs you must scope which mailboxes the app can access (historically via Application Access Policies; newer is Application RBAC). If the app isn’t permitted to that mailbox, auth/send can still fail.

3) Make sure SMTP AUTH is enabled at BOTH tenant + mailbox level

You already enabled it per-mailbox using Set-CASMailbox ... -SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled $false, which is correct.

But there is also a tenant-wide setting. Microsoft documents both levels and the tenant command: Set-TransportConfig -SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled $false (to enable).

Also note: if Security Defaults is enabled, SMTP AUTH is disabled (Microsoft calls this out).

4) Your “smtpUser” string is probably wrong (very common Jakarta Mail bug)

This line:

String smtpUser = mimeMessage.getFrom()[0].toString();

can become something like: "Your Name sender@domain.com"

SMTP AUTH XOAUTH2 expects the UPN/email only. Use:

String smtpUser = ((InternetAddress) mimeMessage.getFrom()[0]).getAddress();

This alone can cause authentication failure even when the token is fine.

5) Use the Jakarta Mail properties that force SASL XOAUTH2 reliably

Jakarta Mail supports XOAUTH2, but it’s safer to enable SASL explicitly (pattern is similar to the JavaMail OAuth2 doc).

Try these props:

props.put("mail.smtp.auth", "true");
props.put("mail.smtp.starttls.enable", "true");
props.put("mail.smtp.host", "smtp.office365.com");
props.put("mail.smtp.port", "587");

props.put("mail.smtp.sasl.enable", "true");
props.put("mail.smtp.sasl.mechanisms", "XOAUTH2");
props.put("mail.smtp.auth.login.disable", "true");
props.put("mail.smtp.auth.plain.disable", "true");
